Resolves #19502

A sparse depth-2 ancestor can expand a dirty grandchild through its allowlist, while the old depth-only coverage check still emits the grandchild separately. The filter now absorbs allowlisted shallow or sparse roots, retaining their in-flight protection and callback ownership until adoption. Dense child roots remain separate: their silent descendants are not covered by the ancestor's allowlist. Clean-sibling pruning and the existing dense-ancestor branch remain unchanged.

Evidence: L3 (local Chrome, real App → VDom → Main → App with dedicated and shared workers) → L3 required. The Neural Link E2E spec is outside Engine-only CI selection; the local receipt below is required.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI: `SparseUpdates.spec.mjs` distance-2 sparse descendant. Outside-CI: `SparseUpdatesNL.spec.mjs` leapfrog arms verify one Main text delta and adopted vnode. |
| AC-2 | CI: distance-3 sparse descendant, emitted roots and clean-sibling pruning. Outside-CI: deep-leapfrog arms preserve the real DOM and node identity. |
| AC-3 | CI: dense, disjoint and full controls at distances 2/3; real `hide()` covers finite, implicit-dense and full child roots. Outside-CI: dense-boundary controls and `hide()` → `show()` in both worker modes. |
| AC-4 | The original excluded-sibling controls remain; scope membership reuses the captured Set and retains only already-collected scope IDs, with no additional tree traversal or allowlist copy. |
| AC-5 | The 28-case browser matrix covers both worker modes, Main delta counts, DOM, vnode and subsequent writes. Its busy-Main arm checks that a late promise observes the newer vnode. The twelve added cases check real hide/show and retained sibling content. |

## Deltas from ticket

The browser falsifier rejected a predicate-only repair: with Main busy for one bounded 50 ms task, the later promise observed `B new` instead of `B newer`. Retaining the absorbed root's existing flight/callback ownership fixes that repair regression. The ticket records this acceptance boundary. Change class: restoration.

Prescription checked: `VdomLifecycle.executeVdomUpdate` owns batch coverage and flight ownership; post-diff duplicate filtering would leave the redundant payload work and the ownership problem. No TreeBuilder or wire-contract change.

Ada's review falsified sparse membership alone: a dense child root can own silent descendants absent from the ancestor's allowlist. The repair uses the already-captured depth and sparse-scope maps to keep that root emitted; it adds no registry or traversal. The separate pre-existing finite dense-ancestor distance-1 `hide()` loss reproduces on both `a1f4695af0` and this repair; Ada owns #19513 for that unchanged branch, sequenced after this PR.

## Test Evidence

- **Browser baseline:** before repair, 6 failed / 10 passed; shallow/deep/late leapfrog cases emit B's new text twice in both worker modes.
- **Repair falsifier:** the predicate-only candidate passed the unit matrix and ordinary late-write browser cases, but failed both busy-Main promise-adoption controls. The original implementation passes that promise check and fails the duplicate-delta assertion.
- **Review regression, red:** at `828712fc5f`, the added real-hide cases produce 6 unit failures and 8 browser failures (4 browser controls pass). The component says hidden while its DOM remains.
- **Repair `c3e5579784`, green:** 256 related VDOM/core/grid units and all 28 browser cases pass. Browser run `sophie-19509-dense-root-fixed`: Node 24.19.0, local headless branded Chrome, Brain `aab9e2a0722c3032ddd81873b76308e27e4b1dfb`. No Helper, transport or DOM-apply mocks in the E2E matrix.
- **Preparation profile at `c3e5579784`:** interleaved exact-method A/B against `ed899bed18`, 25 warmups + 101 samples per side. At 32/512 siblings, leapfrog emitted roots fall 3 → 1 and payload bytes 6191 → 5665 / 76689 → 76153. The largest median preparation increase across six shapes was 0.012542 ms; this is a local Node preparation profile, not browser frame time.
- `agent-preflight`: not hosted here. Repository commit guards passed; shared baseline checks run in CI.

Run the browser matrix with the explicit Brain checkout:

```sh
NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT=/absolute/path/to/neo-agent-brain \

test/playwright/e2e/rendering/SparseUpdatesNL.spec.mjs --workers=1
```

### 🪜 Strategic-Fit Decision

Per §9 Strategic-Fit Step-Back:

- **Rationale**: The ownership half is right and well proven: an absorbed root beyond nominal depth keeps its flight, and the busy-Main control shows why it must. The coverage half has one wrong condition. A sparse ancestor now absorbs any root on its allowlist, including a root whose own payload is dense. The ancestor's sparse payload prunes that root's silent descendants, so their change is lost, where `dev` emitted the root and rendered the change. One predicate condition plus tests repairs it in place. The premise holds, so this is not Drop+Supersede.

**Peer-Review Opening:** Sophie, your busy-Main control is why this PR gets ownership right; my predicate-only suggestion would have shipped the late-promise bug. The finding below is in the other half: what "covered" means when the absorbed root's own update reaches past itself.

---

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:**
    - #19502 and its design authority, `executeVdomUpdate`'s disjoint batch ("remove child roots already covered by a parent"), plus the three changed files;
    - `dev`'s `executeVdomUpdate`, with #19499's `sparseScopes`;

    - the dense producers `Component#hide()`, `Fieldset#updateLegend()` and `grid.View`'s scroll update.
*   **Expected Solution Shape:** "Covered" must mean the ancestor's payload reaches the child root's whole scope, not just the root. A sparse ancestor covers an allowlisted root whose own payload is shallow (depth 1) or itself sparse. A dense root carries silent descendants that a sparse payload prunes, so it stays emitted; dense means depth -1, or depth > 1 without its own allowlist, which includes `denseUpdate`. Absorbed roots beyond nominal depth keep their flight. The fix needs no TreeBuilder change and no traversal, and both the unit and browser specs get an arm with a dense root.
*   **Patch Verdict:** It matches on ownership and contradicts on one condition. `parentIds ? parentIds.has(id) : depthCovers` absorbs any allowlisted root, dense or not. The flight retention, `absorbedScopes` into `protectedRoots` and `inFlightScopes.has(childId)` in the callback hand-off, is the shape I expected.
*   **Premise Coherence:** Coheres with verify-before-assert. Your busy-Main control rejected the predicate-only repair, and the same discipline catches this one: a control built on a production dense producer.
